originality.rationale: The general cost-constrained fastest continuous-time mixing SDP and its geometric dual are explicitly attributed to Sun–Boyd–Xiao–Diaconis. The equal-price star embedding is explicitly attributed to Göring–Helmberg–Wappler. What remains assessed is the unique all-heterogeneous-price closed-form star solution, polygon regime boundary, and eigenvalue multiplicity switch, not the general optimization mechanism, uniform-price special case, or an arbitrary-price algorithm. No equal or stronger explicit star statement was identified in the inspected primary text or searched mathematical records; incomplete historical coverage is acknowledged.
residual_risks: The specialized heterogeneously priced star solution might already have been deduced in obscure or unindexed maximum-variance embedding literature.
The full text of Fiedler (1990) was not accessible here; it is known from its abstract to treat uniform-price tree optimization, but a full comparison was not possible.

General SDP theory makes the closed-form result derivable in principle; originality rests on the explicit all-price formula, strict uniqueness, phase criterion and multiplicity analysis rather than a new general framework.

value.rationale: Arbitrary continuous heterogeneous price inputs admit a unique globally optimal set of weighted-star conductances with no numerical SDP. The sharp polygon inequality identifies a genuinely unexpected region in which equal conductances remain optimal despite unequal prices; outside, the exact reallocation pattern and eigenspace dimension switch. This offers interpretable design sensitivities for continuous-time diffusion and goes beyond the previously known equal-price star and generic algorithmic formulations.
